observes: Disconnect world, ledger commit, AUDITIA, IRIS 2026.1 Community, client through a TCP proxy that frames the IRIS wire protocol, SIGKILL + both sockets closed at an exact message; 15 trials + 1 baseline, 0 violations of O1-O6 (judged again by pg-disconnect-reevaluate). A1 (caller START TRANSACTION, ledger.commit of 300 relationships applied at a nested level, driver COMMIT 'TC' dropped) 3/3 nothing: the dead server process's transaction was undone (journal: one span, 10,511 writes and 10,511 compensating records, net zero), the revision the client had been answered inside its transaction (seq, id) does not exist and the same-key retry committed it fresh once (same seq, new id). A2 (7,000 relationships, staged: 2 StageChunk requests reached the server, Commit dropped) 3/3 nothing, nothing journaled, retry committed once. A3 (6,000 relationships, Commit cut 0.30 s after forwarding, reply pending) 3/3 full: the server ran the call to its end and exited 5.4-6.4 s after the kill (18,000 records committed); the retry replayed the revision the state holds. B1 (Commit reply held) 3/3 full, retry replayed=True with the held reply's seq and revision id. B2 (caller transaction, the COMMIT's reply held) 3/3 full, retry replayed the first answer. Head lock free after every kill and retry (15/15); verify equal 15/15; content exactly once 15/15. SynchCommit=0; no crash here.
